name: A square and a point inside
Points on an edge
why: [(0, 0), (2, 0), (2, 2), (0, 2)]. (1, 0) and (1, 2) lie on edges, not at corners, so they are left out: pop when the cross product is ≤ 0, not only < 0.

name: The lowest, then the leftmost
why: [(1, 0), (3, 0), (5, 2), (2, 4), (0, 1)]. Two points have the lowest y, 0; the answer starts at the left one, (1, 0).

name: All on one line
why: [(0, 0), (5, 5)]: only the two ends are corners.

name: A triangle full of points
why: [(0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 4)]: many points inside and on the edges, three corners.

name: 100,000 points, all corners
expr: (lambda r: [len(r), r[:3], r[-3:], sum(x * 31 + y for x, y in r) % 1000000007])(hull(list(args[0])))
show: the points (x, x²) for x = −50000 .. 49999, in a scrambled order
why: [how many, first three, last three, a check number]. Every point is a corner. Gift wrapping costs O(n · h), about 10 billion steps here; the monotone chain is O(n log n).

name: 200,000 random points
expr: (lambda r: [len(r), r[:3], r[-3:], sum(x * 31 + y for x, y in r) % 1000000007])(hull(list(args[0])))
show: 200,000 random points in a square of side 10⁹
why: Few corners, many points. Sorting dominates: O(n log n).
